conviction_note: No company-level number the market has not seen was found: the print is a no-call, no-guidance quarter for a $47m office REIT trading at about 8% of book equity, and the stock is rising into it (+50% off the 5 Oct low of $0.30, +15% in 5 days) on a public 13D buyer's accumulation. I lean slightly down (p_up 45) on that run-up and on 5 of 7 prior prints falling. abs_move_pct is 6.0, above the 4.5% median, because a $0.01 tick is 2.2% and 20-day realised vol is 84.5%. The findings sum to -0.3, close to the scaled -0.6. Both are near zero because the strategic-process tail is two-sided and has no date.
bar: Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS/FFO consensus $0.02 from one source (Benzinga, page last updated 2026-09-16: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSP/earnings-forecasts). There is no company guide (the Q2 release gives none) and no second agreeing estimate, so the bar is effectively unsourced and every finding is capped small. Q2 FFO was $1.6m ($0.015, printed as $0.02) on 104.0m shares. Q3 loses Greenwood Plaza's NOI (sold 2026-07-08) and saves about $0.19m of interest from the $8.5m paydown, so FFO of about $0.01-0.02 is expected. The stock does not trade on FFO.
positioning_check: Short interest 1,104,307 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 1.1% of the 104.0m shares, 1.0 days to cover, down from 1,406,916 at 09-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/fsp/short-interest?range=3m, read 2026-10-27). This is not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze mechanism. Options: empty chain (baseline), so there is no skew and no implied move. The baseline anchor is the 4.51% median of 7 prior reactions (2 up, 5 down). Run-up: +25% over 20 days, +15.4% over 5 days, -66% from the 52-week high. A new 6.8% holder (Powell Anderson Capital, 13D filed 2026-10-14) was buying through 10-14 at $0.31-0.39. BofA holds a passive 5.2% under a 13G; BofA Securities is also a co-advisor on the strategic process.

findings.finding: A new 13D (filed 2026-10-14, event date 2026-10-06) shows Powell Anderson Capital Partners / PACP Acadia / R. Adam Lindsay holding 7,067,763 shares (6.8% of 104,011,708). They paid about $2.9m in open-market purchases from 2026-08-17 to 2026-10-14 at $0.31-0.48, mostly $0.31-0.39. Item 4 says the shares were 'undervalued and represented an attractive investment opportunity' and reserves the right to engage with the board on business combinations and dispositions. No letter and no demand. For comparison, the stock was $0.39 on the filing date and $0.45 now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior 13D reaction in the baseline. The earlier activist (Converium/Erez, 6.8%, Nov 2024) ended in a cooperation agreement and a board seat, and the stock still fell from about $1.6 to $0.45 over the following 18 months.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The filing is 13 days old and the stock is up about 15% since. What is not priced is that a holder with a $0.31-0.39 cost base and a stated value thesis is a likely bid on any post-print dip, which damps the downside tail of the reaction. If the market had fully discounted that support, the stock would not have sold off on 5 of 7 prior prints with no such holder present.
findings.independence: Exhibit 99.2 of the same filing (Schedule A trade list, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1031316/000121465926012926/ex99_2.htm) is the same document and does not count as separate evidence. No independent corroboration was found: no news coverage or letter from Powell Anderson turned up.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print +50% off its 2026-10-05 close of $0.30, at $0.45. It is +15.4% over 5 days and +25% over 20 days, on rising volume (4.0m shares on 10-12, about 0.9-1.1m a day on 10-21 to 10-26 against a 20-day average of 1.12m). The company has put out nothing since the 13D apart from the 10-20 date notice. The base case for a no-call, no-guide release is a quarter with no strategic outcome, and 5 of FSP's last 7 prints fell (-8.33% Mar-26, -4.55% Apr-26, 0.0% Jul-26, when the stock had run +9% on the print day).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 2 of 7 up, median |move| 4.51%. The Jul-26 print came after a +9% day into the release and moved 0.0%. Mar-26 (dividend suspension) -8.33%. Apr-26 -4.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is a price, so this finding argues that the price is ahead of the news flow. If the market expected nothing from the release, the stock would have stayed near the $0.38-0.40 level it held after the 13D. Holding $0.45 implies some hope of a strategic update, and that update has no date.
findings.independence: None from a different source. This rests on the same tape the baseline carries.

findings.finding: The 2026-10-20 notice says there will be no conference call or webcast for Q3, the same as Q2. A company announcing a corporate or portfolio transaction alongside results would normally explain it on a call, so the absence of one mildly lowers the odds that a strategic outcome lands in this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 also had no call, and the reaction was 0.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The fact is on the wire. What may not be priced is the inference that no transaction is likely, given that the stock has risen 15% since the notice.
findings.independence: None. This is an inference from an absence and is filed small.

findings.finding: Leased % has drifted down for three quarters: 69.2% (Mar-25), 68.9% (Dec-25), 68.4% (Mar-26), 67.4% (Jun-26), with expirations exceeding new leases. Only 143,154 sq ft (about 3%) of 2026 expirations remain in the year, against 551,951 sq ft (11.5%) in 2027. So Q3 occupancy is likely flat to slightly down. The 2027 renewal disclosure in the supplemental is the line to watch. FFO is likely $0.01-0.02 against the single-source $0.02 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Occupancy slipped 0.5pt in Q1 (-4.55%) and 1.0pt in Q2 (0.0%), so this line has not moved the stock reliably.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock trades at about 0.08x book on vacancy. The 2027 expiration wall (11.5%) is public, but how much of it has been renewed will first be visible in this supplemental.
findings.independence: Q1 supplemental (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031316/000110465926050393/fsp-20260428xex99d2.htm) shows the same downward trend. That is the same company series, not independent.

findings.finding: Liquidity and covenants do not look like a print-day trigger. Cash and restricted cash were $22.5m at 6/30, plus about $8.9m kept from the Greenwood sale, against a $5.0m minimum-liquidity covenant. There is a $45m delayed-draw facility for TI/LC (lender approval needed, undrawn). Book equity of $580.0m sits against a $424.9m minimum tangible net worth covenant, with a step-down for impairments and disposals. The $275m TPG loan carries 9% cash interest, no amortization and matures Feb-2029. EDGAR full-text search finds no 'substantial doubt' language in any 2026 filing. H1 burn was -$2.1m operating cash and -$5.8m capex.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb-2026 refinance was followed by the Mar-26 print at -8.33%, which carried the dividend suspension, so the stock has sold off on capital-preservation news before.
findings.why_not_priced: At 8% of book a distress tail is priced. The 10-Q shows that tail is not near-term: covenant headroom of about $155m and cash cover of more than six quarters at the H1 burn rate. If the market were pricing a covenant event, the 13D buyer would not have accumulated and short interest would not have fallen to 1.1%.
findings.independence: The EDGAR full-text search for 'substantial doubt' (CIK 1031316, 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-27) returned no hits: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22substantial%20doubt%22&ciks=0001031316&dateRange=custom&startdt=2026-01-01&enddt=2026-10-27

findings.finding: JLL's Q3 2026 US office report (published 2026-10-13) shows a fifth straight quarter of positive net absorption (+6.0m sq ft in Q3, +21m sq ft YTD). It says Sun Belt and tertiary markets have recovered to more than 95% of 2019 leasing volume. That is mildly supportive of FSP's Sunbelt/Mountain West leasing in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no record of FSP reacting to macro office data. Its own leased % fell through the 2025-26 recovery.
findings.why_not_priced: The macro series is public. FSP's own leased % has not tracked it, so the market is right to discount the transmission.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Piedmont's Sept-2026 conference (Sunbelt, 72% of ALR) guided 2026 leasing of 1.7-2.0m sq ft and rising net effective rents (https://quartr.com/events/piedmont-office-realty-trust-inc-pdm-bofa-securities-real-estate-conference-presentation_ofZW7JHP), but that is a peer, not FSP.

findings.finding: The strategic review (since May 2025, formally expanded in April 2026 with BofA Securities and JLL as co-advisors) is now six months past its relaunch with no outcome disclosed. Its scope covers 'potential corporate transactions, portfolio level transactions, individual asset dispositions'. At $0.45 the market values equity at about $47m against $580m of book equity. Real estate is carried at $758m net against $275m of debt (plus a 4% prepayment exit fee). Any corporate or portfolio deal announced with the release, even well below book, would be a very large positive. An update showing only small asset sales or impairments on marketed assets would be negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The process expansion (2026-04-23) and the Feb-2026 'refinance as the best alternative' update both came between prints. Neither the Q1 nor the Q2 print carried a transaction, and those prints moved -4.55% and 0.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced as a low-probability option. The stock at 0.08x book shows the market assigns little chance of a deal. The tail is filed because a timing coincidence with the release is possible and nobody can source it. If a leak had occurred, the volume on 10-12/10-13 (4.0m and 2.4m shares) would be the sign, and those days line up with the 13D buyer's purchases rather than with news.
findings.independence: The 13D buyer's stated value thesis (first finding) is a separate document pointing the same way, but it is not evidence of timing. No 8-K 1.01 or 2.01 has been filed since 2026-07-13.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to read. My slight negative agrees with the name's 5-of-7 down print history and cuts against the +15% 5-day run-up only in the sense that it bets on that run-up fading. A low 1.1% short interest and a new value holder bidding below the price argue against sizing it larger.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (inference from an absence is worth little): the no-call finding was shrunk from -0.3 to -0.2. It is kept because it is sourced and filed small.
Lesson 6 (bar has one source): the single-source $0.02 bar is now stated as capping all findings. Sizes were already small and are left unchanged.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): checked that the liquidity finding is signed on covenant headroom and the absence of going-concern language. Left at +0.2.
Lesson 7 (positioning, short interest before negatives): short interest of 1.1% / 1.0 days to cover was looked up before the run-up negative. It is not crowded, so the -1.5 stands.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, understatement): abs_move_pct kept at 6.0, above the 4.51% median. Unchanged.
